name: Unexplained Absence
oracle_text: For each player, exile up to one target nonland permanent that player controls. For each permanent exiled this way, its controller cloaks the top card of their library. (To cloak a card, put it onto the battlefield face down as a 2/2 creature with ward {2}. Turn it face up any time for its mana cost if it's a creature card.)
blocked_sentences: For each permanent exiled this way, its controller cloaks the top card of their library. (To cloak a card, put it onto the battlefield face down as a 2/2 creature with ward {2}. Turn it face up any time for its mana cost if it's a creature card.)
For each player, exile up to one target nonland permanent that player controls

needs.what: Face-down permanents. A card leaves a hidden zone (here the top of a library) and enters the battlefield face down as a colorless 2/2 creature with no name, no types beyond Creature, no mana cost and ward {2}, while the engine keeps the real card underneath; its controller may turn it face up at any time -- a special action, not a spell or ability, so it uses no stack -- by paying the real card's mana cost, but only if the real card is a creature card, at which point every printed characteristic replaces the 2/2 shell. Needs (a) a face-down flag on a battlefield object whose characteristics are the 2/2 shell rather than the underlying card, (b) an op that moves library-top / hand / exile cards to the battlefield in that state, targeting a chosen player's library, (c) a turn-face-up special action offered as a decision at any priority, gated on the hidden card's real type and cost, and (d) ward {2} as a real keyword.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `put_onto_battlefield` is the closest op, but it puts the card onto the battlefield as itself -- there is no face-down state, so the permanent would be the real card with its printed name, types and P/T, publicly visible, which is a different card. `create_token` can make a 2/2 body but a token is not the library card: the real card must stay underneath to be turned face up later, and it must leave the library (`library_size` changes), which a token does not do. `set_pt` and `animate` override characteristics only on an already face-up permanent and cannot hide identity. `transform` swaps between two *printed* faces of a double-faced card, which is not the same as a generic face-down shell over an arbitrary card. `grant_keyword` cannot supply ward: `ward` is absent from the packet's `keywords` list, and the engine already treats it as a parameterised/unimplemented keyword (see the "ward {2}" comments in src/automtg/cards/authoring/templates.py and src/automtg/cards/proxy.py). Finally there is no special-action decision kind: everything a player may do "any time" today is an activated ability that goes on the stack from the battlefield.

needs.what: A target requirement that instantiates once per player at cast time -- "for each player, exile up to one target nonland permanent that player controls" -- so the number of optional targets scales with the size of the pod and each target is constrained to a *different* player's permanents. Also needs the resolving effect to identify, per exiled permanent, which player controlled it, so the follow-on clause can act on that player.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `targets` is a fixed list of `TargetSpec` written at authoring time (see TargetSpec in src/automtg/engine/carddef.py: id, kind, selector, count, optional). `optional: true` gives "up to one", and `controller` in a selector gives "you" or "opponent", so a hand-written pair of specs reproduces the card only in a two-player game; in a four-player Commander game -- which is what this card is printed for -- it would silently offer two targets instead of four. That is an approximation, not the card.
